Their flux peaks in the near-infrared, beyond the wavelength cut-off of the silicon-based CCDs used by ground-based surveys dedicated to observing them, such as SPECULOOS. We present the on-sky performance of SPIRIT (SPeculoos InfraRed Imager for Transits), an InGaAs CMOS detector on the Callisto telescope at the SPECULOOS Southern Observatory, during its first year of operation, from mid-2022 to 2023. We use 328 visits of 73 targets to optimise our CMOS-specific reduction process, including our approach to glow effects and bad-pixel handling. We find the measured precision to be consistent with our theoretical noise model, achieving sub-part-per-thousand precision under good observing conditions across targets spanning $J$-band magnitudes of 10--13. We further illustrate SPIRIT's capabilities with two case studies: a simultaneous SPIRIT $zYJ$ and CCD $I + z$ observation of a TRAPPIST-1\,h transit, and monitoring observations of the fast-rotating dwarf LP~944-20. Our results confirm that InGaAs infrared CMOS detectors are a cost-effective and competitive technology for ground-based transit photometry of cool stars, and that they show promising prospects to become a core part of the next generation of instruments.

papers.title: Low-cost neural summaries for cosmological inference: an ensemble of convolutional neural networks trained on approximate simulations
papers.abstract: Machine learning can build near-optimal summary statistics for extracting cosmological information from the large-scale structure of the Universe. Training them, however, requires large numbers of costly simulations. We aim to build a neural summary trained on fast, approximate low-resolution simulations that remains informative when applied to higher-resolution ones, reducing the cost of the training set. We train an ensemble of convolutional neural networks with different architectures to compress the matter overdensity fields of low-resolution particle-mesh simulations. The outputs of a subset of networks are concatenated into a summary statistic, which we use to constrain $Ω_{\rm m}$ and $σ_8$ from high-resolution particle-mesh simulations, each about a thousand times more costly than their low-resolution counterparts. Theoretical predictions are provided by a Gaussian process emulator built from the high-resolution simulations. We test three strategies for selecting the smallest informative subset of networks. Constraints are compared with those from a reference power spectrum analysis. We also consider dark matter halo catalogues from independent high-resolution $N$-body simulations. The neural summary extracts information beyond the binned power spectrum. Using multiple networks is essential: a single network can be less informative than the power spectrum. A greedy search based on posterior volume provides the tightest constraints with the fewest networks. The neural summary also outperforms the power spectrum for dark matter haloes, at different number densities and redshifts, despite being trained on low-resolution matter fields at $z=0$. This work demonstrates that an ensemble of networks trained on approximate simulations yields a summary statistic that remains informative on higher-fidelity data, including dark matter haloes. (Abridged)

papers.title: PDRs4All XXIII. JWST-MIRI template spectra of PAHs in the Orion Bar obtained with blind signal separation
papers.abstract: The aromatic infrared bands (AIBs) are observed in a wide variety of astrophysical sources, and now in unprecedented detail by the James Webb space telescope (JWST). These bands are generally attributed to the emission from polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAHs). Our aim is to extract mid-infrared AIB template spectra from JWST observations of the Orion Bar photo-dissociation region that can be used to derive PAH properties from observations of other objects. We used the JWST MIRI-MRS observations from the PDRs4All program. We first isolated the AIBs from the data using a multi-component fitting approach. We then applied a non-negative matrix factorization to the isolated AIB spectra and extracted two templates, named AIBirrad and AIBshield following previous work. The spatial distribution and spectral characteristics of these two spectra suggest that they originate from two chemical distinct populations. We interpret AIBirrad as emission originating from a PAH population strongly exposed to ultra-violet (UV) radiation and mainly composed of large, compact ionized PAHs. Conversely, AIBshield is interpreted as originating from a more shielded population of PAHs, which is less exposed to the UV by being more embedded in the cloud. This population consists of small, asymmetric and mainly neutral PAHs with bonded aliphatic side groups. These templates can serve to analyze PAH emission in a wide variety of objects observed with MIRI-MRS.

papers.title: Black Hole Binary Mergers in Galactic Nuclei: Combined Effects of Secular Dynamics and Stellar Flybys
papers.abstract: Galactic nuclei, with the central supermassive black holes (SMBHs) and surrounding dense star clusters, serve as natural laboratories for studying gravitational dynamics in extreme gravitational environments. In this work, we model the long term evolution of black hole binaries (BHBs) in these environments by incorporating the tidal influence of the central SMBH, the potential of the nuclear star cluster, SMBH induced relativistic precession, and stochastic perturbations from stellar flybys. Our numerical simulations show that the long term evolution of BHBs is predominantly governed by the SMBH-driven ZLK mechanism. However, once stellar flybys are included, they can modify both the binary angular momentum and energy. The cumulative effect of repeated flyby encounters substantially reshapes the long term dynamical evolution, eventually leading systems toward either merger or disruption. Based on a population synthesis study, we find that this combined secular and non-secular channel produces a merger rate of approximately $\mathcal{R}\simeq16\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}yr^{-1}}$, which is significantly higher than the rates predicted by dynamical channels that neglect stellar flybys. Furthermore, we predict that a non-negligible fraction of merging systems would retain detectable eccentricities at low frequencies around 5 Hz, thus providing a distinctive observational signature for next generation ground based GW detectors. Our results demonstrate that the stochastic perturbations from the surrounding environment are essential for modeling BHB evolution in galactic nuclei, and that this channel may contribute a major fraction of observed mergers.

papers.title: Linear Polarization of Synchrotron Radiation from Very-small-pitch-angle Electrons
papers.abstract: For synchrotron radiation with pitch angle $α\ll 1/γ$ where $γ$ is the electron Lorentz factor, referred to as very-small-pitch-angle synchrotron radiation, the polarization properties differ significantly from those of conventional synchrotron radiation ($α\gg 1/γ$). In this work, we investigate the linear polarization characteristics of very-small-pitch-angle synchrotron radiation from relativistic thermal and nonthermal electrons. We calculate the linear polarization by applying power-law and Maxwellian electron energy distributions. Moreover, some synchrotron sources exhibit a hybrid distribution of nonthermal and thermal electrons, and we also calculate the polarization degree for a hybrid electron energy distribution. The calculations are performed in the radio, optical, X-ray, and $γ$-ray bands. Our results show that the linear polarization degree of very-small-pitch-angle synchrotron radiation is generally lower than that of conventional synchrotron radiation. Very-small-pitch-angle synchrotron radiation from both nonthermal and thermal electrons can produce significant linear polarization. However, the polarization exhibits diverse behaviors across different physical parameters. The general scenario provided in this work can be considered for the application to all kinds of synchrotron sources, as we suggest that the very-small-pitch-angle case is crucial for the study of synchrotron polarization.

papers.title: LiDO: The Large inclination Distant Objects Survey
papers.abstract: Previous trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs) discovery surveys targeted the ecliptic plane, where the overall highest density is seen. High-inclination objects spend little time near the plane, and are thus under-represented in previous TNO surveys. The Large inclination Distant Objects (LiDO) survey targets these high-inclination populations in 34 sq.deg., located in two blocks 14-21 degrees north and south of the ecliptic plane, finding 148 objects, all with i>14 degrees due to survey design. A careful characterization of detection efficiency and other survey parameters results in a "characterized sample" of 125 objects detected within the survey's magnitude and rate limits, thus suitable for model comparison via survey simulations. LiDO detected 62 TNOs classified as resonant, including 21 Plutinos, of which 12 are securely Kozai resonators (always coming to pericenter off-ecliptic), as well as 9 objects in the 5:2 resonance, and several mixed mode inclination-eccentricity resonators. No objects beyond 63 au were detected, despite sensitivity to objects as far as 150 au. We found that the i>14 degree orbital distribution of the previous model from OSSOS was rejectable with the inclusion of the 38 characterized hot classical TNOs from LiDO. We constructed a proof-of-concept orbital distribution model of hot classical TNOs based on long-term stability sculpting, which is statistically acceptable for the LiDO and OSSOS samples, while producing population estimates (21,000$^{+3000}_{-3000}$ hot classicals with H_r<8.3) consistent with OSSOS estimates. The discovery of 125 characterized mid-to-high inclination objects in a variety of orbital classifications provides useful constraints for population modeling and the migration history of the Solar System.

papers.title: specwizard: A Public Python Framework for Creating Synthetic Absorption Spectra from Hydrodynamical Simulations
papers.abstract: We present specwizard, a publicly available modular Python package for generating synthetic absorption spectra from hydrodynamical simulations. The code combines atomic data from the National Institute of Standards and Technology database with ionisation fractions computed using the cloudy spectral synthesis code for multiple ionising backgrounds, enabling consistent modelling of bound--bound and bound--free absorption for resonant transitions of all ions. specwizard employs a column-density--conserving projection scheme, includes natural line broadening for the Lyman series, and offers optional treatments of instrumental resolution and noise for direct comparison with high-resolution quasar spectra. As example applications of the code, we shoot sightlines through the eagle cosmological simulation to generate a z = 3.2 synthetic quasar spectrum containing H i Lyman-series transitions, including damping wings and Lyman-limit absorption. Additionally, we compute metal-absorption lines probing the circumgalactic medium of simulated galaxies, and investigate the correlated absorption of H i and Si iii. We demonstrate that specwizard applied to outputs from eagle accurately reproduces key observational diagnostics of the Lyman-alpha forest, including the redshift evolution of the mean transmission, the transmission PDF and the transmission power spectrum. We take advantage of the fact that the eagle simulation also reproduces the measured evolution of the temperature-density relation to infer the evolution of the amplitude of the ionizing background, finding excellent agreement with recent theoretical models and measurements.

papers.title: A heterogeneous set of unusual quasars selected from astrometry and broad-band photometry
papers.abstract: The aim of this study is to explore methods for how to identify new quasars with different properties with regard to reddening, redshift, the presence of broad absorption lines from outflows, or other rare properties affecting the broad-band colours. We use Gaia-based astrometric pre-selection to study only sources that have zero parallax and zero proper motion within errors. We subsequently match these sources with information from wide-area photometric surveys and build colour-colour diagrams. Based on these diagrams we select targets for follow-up spectroscopy. In the subsequent analysis we also apply observations from SPHEREx to firmly establish redshifts. We secure spectroscopic observations for 24 sources. Of these, three are found to be stars and the remaining 21 are classified as quasars spanning a redshift range from z=0.139 to z=3.732. The majority of the sources located away from the normal quasar locus in colour-colour diagrams are found to be broad-absorption-line quasars. A single source, the lowest redshift source at z=0.139, is reminiscent of the so-called Little Red Dots found at high redshifts with JWST. Using the simple procedure followed here it is possible to locate previously undiscovered quasars with interesting properties, in particular Broad Absorption Line quasars and quasars with unusual extinction.

papers.title: Strong gravitational lensing with Euclid
papers.abstract: Euclid data is going to lead to the discovery of approximately 10^5 new strong gravitational lenses, thereby increasing the number of known lenses by a factor of 30. Such an impressive jump has the potential to revolutionise the field of strong lensing, by covering an ever-increasing range in the parameter space occupied by the lenses and lensed sources, and by uncovering rare and precious strong lens systems. The first quick data release of Euclid has already revealed hundreds of lenses, giving us a taste of what the final Euclid strong lens sample might look like. These lenses include a variety of objects acting as deflectors, from isolated galaxies to clusters, from early-type galaxies to edge-on disks. As many as four double-source plane lenses, in which one foreground object lenses two galaxies at two different redshifts, have already been discovered. As more data are acquired, it might become possible to detect the strong lensing signature of dwarf galaxy satellites, and to find lenses with an unusually large number of images. In this paper, we try to anticipate the kind of discoveries that these data will bring along.

papers.title: Large dust grains escaping from a supernova remnant
papers.abstract: Dust grains produced in the supernova (SN) ejecta at early ages are partially destroyed in hot gas of the SN remnant. Large grains owing to their inertia can overtake the forward shock front of the remnant and move through the ambient interstellar medium. Using one-dimensional gas dynamics including the dust destruction we study the transport of dust grains inside the SN remnant and the ambient medium. Here we estimate the surviving and escaping mass fractions depending on the cut-off (maximum) size in a power-law distribution of grain sizes. We found that these fractions follow closely each other at late age of the SN remnant, i.e. almost all grains, which have survived in the remnant, leave it for the ambient interstellar medium. At the age of 30 kyr -- the onset of the radiative phase with density $n\sim 1$ cm$^{-3}$ with solar metallicity -- the escaping/surviving mass fractions for the cut-off size of several microns reach about $0.7-0.8$. The major part of these grains have size larger than $1~μ$m and initially located at distances $\gtrsim 0.2$ of the ejecta core radius. Later dust grains at velocity of several hundreds km/s escaping the remnant continue to be destroyed due to kinetic sputtering in the interstellar medium. Grains with sizes of several microns are destroyed marginally and therefore will survive in the interstellar gas. After decelerating of grains in the medium the surviving mass fraction of grains produced in the SN remnant, which evolves in an ambient gas with $n$ from 1 to 100 cm$^{-3}$, is from $\sim 0.5$ to $\sim 0.3$, respectively, for the cut-off grain size $a_{cut} = 10~μ$m. A decrease of the cut-off size in the distribution results in lower surviving mass fraction.

papers.title: Identifying Planetary Nebulae Candidates from IPHAS and VPHAS+ Surveys via YOLO Deep Learning Models
papers.abstract: We present a deep learning detection method capable of effectively identifying planetary nebulae (PNe) on IPHAS and VPHAS+ surveys. Our detection pipeline is based on the YOLO architecture and is adaptable to other datasets. Using the HiPS system, we preprocess and augment the $r$, $i$, and $Hα$ bands to produce two red, green, and blue (RGB) image datasets: (1) $640 \times 640$ px images at full resolution, and (2) $1 280 \times 1 280$ px images designed to capture extended objects up to $0.2$ deg. Images of $\sim 2600$ PNe are labelled using the HASH database. The loss function and evaluation metrics are adapted to the diffuse and low-contrast nature of PNe; a very low intersection over union (IoU) threshold ($1\%$) is used. A $k$-fold cross validation shows that the YOLOv12m model achieves an average precision of $0.979$ on the first dataset. At a confidence threshold of $0.15$, it achieves a precision rate of $98.7\%$ and a recall rate of $97.4\%$. We deployed our system (on $1280 \times 1280$ images) on the full surveys' coverage ($\sim 3755$ deg$^2$), and present a preliminary analysis of the detection results. The system is robust against artifacts such as CCD corner defects and HiPS tile joints. Our convolutional-neural-network-based model achieved excellent results on the test set, comparable to-or exceeding-that of a recent Swin Transformer approach. However, a challenge persists when applying deep learning models to extensive and densely populated Galactic fields: the development of an automated system that can effectively discriminate PNe from mimics that human experts are able to distinguish (e.g., H II regions). We outline possible improvements for future work.

papers.title: High-Frequency Transverse Waves in Chromospheric Fibrils Revealed by DKIST
papers.abstract: Chromospheric fibrils are ubiquitous dynamical structures that can support magnetohydrodynamic waves and may contribute to energy transport in the solar atmosphere. Using high-resolution observations from the Visible Broadband Imager (VBI) onboard the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST), we investigate transverse oscillations of H$α$ fibrils. Our observations encompass both quiet-Sun and active regions. The results reveal that high-frequency transverse oscillations are highly prevalent in fibrils across different magnetic environments. The detected oscillations exhibit typical periods of 56 $\pm$ 49 s, displacement amplitudes of 37 $\pm$ 25 km, velocity amplitudes of 6 $\pm$ 4 km\,s$^{-1}$, and phase velocities of 21 $\pm$ 13 km\,s$^{-1}$. Under typical chromospheric conditions, the estimated wave energy flux ranges from 20 to 200 W\,m$^{-2}$. The characteristics of these transverse oscillations are consistent with those of Alfvénic kink-mode waves. Our results reveal the existence of the high-frequency, small-amplitude transverse waves in chromospheric fibrils and providing new constraints on their contribution to the chromospheric and coronal heating.

papers.title: Evidence for Suppressed Non-thermal Broadening in a Flare Ribbon from Stereoscopic Observations
papers.abstract: Flare ribbons mark the footpoints of newly reconnected magnetic loops and are commonly associated with strong plasma flows and enhanced non-thermal broadening of transition-region lines due to impulsive energy deposition. However, the mechanisms governing energy transport into flare ribbons remain uncertain, particularly under different magnetic field configurations. We investigate the energy deposition process at a flare ribbon near a sunspot by determining the physical nature of its small-scale downflows. We study small-scale downflows in a remote ribbon during the M7.7-class event on 30 September 2024, using coordinated observations from SDO, IRIS, and Solar Orbiter. We use stereoscopic imaging from Solar Orbiter and IRIS to detect plane-of-sky motions on small scales (200 km). We conduct spectroscopic analysis of IRIS Si IV profiles, complemented by C II and Mg II diagnostics. Apparent downflow speeds measured from Solar Orbiter imaging (limb view) are 85-130 km/s, while IRIS images (disk view) reveal plane-of-sky speeds of 70-85 km/s. In contrast, IRIS Si IV profiles at the brightest ribbon pixels are well approximated by a single Gaussian, with minimal Doppler shifts and unexpectedly small non-thermal widths (10 km/s). Peak Si IV emission also coincides with a deeper Mg II central reversal, while electron densities are one to two orders of magnitude higher than typical quiet-Sun values. The absence of significant line-of-sight velocities and non-thermal broadening differs from typical flare-ribbon behavior. Our results are consistent with a scenario in which plasma motions are guided by highly inclined (nearly horizontal) magnetic fields in chromospheric canopy and are not accompanied by strong turbulence or wave motions. This study suggests that flare ribbons can exhibit a wide diversity of lower-atmospheric responses and emphasizes the critical role of magnetic field geometry.

papers.title: Microcaustics: Fast GPU-Accelerated Dynamical Microlensing of Time-Dependent Extended Sources
papers.abstract: Gravitational microlensing probes unresolved quasar accretion disc structure and compact objects in lens galaxies and is an important systematic in strong-lens time-delay cosmography. Most analyses use static microlensing map simulations because evolving individual microlenses and caustics is computationally prohibitive. We present Microcaustics, a GPU-accelerated Python package built on PyTorch for dynamical microlensing of time-dependent extended sources in strong gravitational lenses. It combines a local-exact/far-field deflection solver, source-directed lens-plane scouting with temporal reuse, and biquadratic inverse polygon mapping (IPM). GPU batching and fused Triton rasterization accelerate the calculation, while binary caustic labels track source-centred crossings. Across three simulated quadruply lensed quasar systems, our package generates a 10-year, 147-frame multiband light curve in an amortized median of 0.68 s (0.88 s with labels) on a consumer GPU with a median light-curve RMSE of 0.35 mmag, while recovering every reference source-centred caustic crossing. At comparable map accuracy, the batched throughput is 780 times higher than that of a recent CUDA IPM implementation and extrapolates to a speedup of millions relative to classic GPU-D. We demonstrate that our IPM converges as $N_{\rm ray}^{-0.84}$, approaching the idealized $N_{\rm ray}^{-1}$ convergence rate of piecewise-affine IPM and improving upon the $N_{\rm ray}^{-1/2}$ inverse ray-shooting rate. We also introduce a GPU-resident general relativistic and reverberating quasar source model and demonstrate our method with an evolving supernova source. These advances make fully dynamical stellar fields practical for Bayesian and simulation-based inference.

papers.title: Constraint on particle mass of dark matter based on XTE J1814-338 observation and DANS model
papers.abstract: The small observed radius of neutron star XTE J1814-338 (with mass of $1.21_{-0.05}^{+0.05}$ $M_{\odot}$ and radius of $7_{-0.4}^{+0.4}$ $\rm{km}$) poses a great challenge to the traditional neutron star model composed of normal nuclear matter. The dark matter admixed neutron star (DANS) model provides a clue to solve this challenge. By employing the self-interacting fermionic dark matter model, we investigate the effects of dark matter parameters including the particle mass, self-interaction strength, and mass fraction of dark matter on the properties of DANSs. Our results indicate that the joint constraints from the observation of XTE J1814-338 and the astrophysical limits on the dark matter self-interaction cross section derived from observations of different colliding galaxy clusters can provide effective constraints on the particle mass of dark matter. Specifically, to simultaneously satisfy the small radius of XTE J1814-338 and the self-interaction limit, the particle mass of self-interacting fermionic dark matter is constrained to the range from sub-GeV to a few GeV.

papers.title: Post-merger rotational evolution of magnetised single hot subdwarfs results in slow rotation due to magnetic braking
papers.abstract: Single hot subdwarfs are believed to form through mergers of helium-core white dwarfs, which can lead to large-scale magnetic fields generated during the merger, and may be observable at the surface once they evolve into the stable core-helium burning phase. As a post-merger product, the orbital angular momentum of the binary system that forms it, could lead to a rapidly rotating hot subdwarf. But previous models were not able to explain the rather slow rotational velocities of observed single hot subdwarfs. Motivated by recent detections of surface magnetic fields in hot subdwarfs in the range 200 - 500 kiloGauss, we explore in this work the role of large-scale magnetic fields on their rotational evolution via rotating stellar evolution models. We find that large-scale stable magnetic fields can extract angular momentum efficiently from the star via coupling to stellar winds, producing slowly rotating single hot subdwarfs and thus providing a possible explanation to both the long rotation periods provided by asteroseismology and low spectroscopic rotational velocities. This hints magnetic braking could be an important component of the rotational properties of low-mass stellar mergers.

papers.title: Correlation of galactic very-high-energy gamma-ray sources detected by LHAASO with high-energy neutrinos
papers.abstract: We conducted an investigation into the possible correlation between very-high-energy (VHE, $E>$ 0.1 TeV) gamma-ray sources, as identified by the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO), and high-energy neutrino events captured by the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. For this analysis, we utilized the First LHAASO catalog, which comprises 90 VHE gamma-ray sources, and the IceCube Event Catalog of Alert Tracks (IceCat-1), which includes 348 track-like neutrino events. Through Monte Carlo simulations, we assessed the correlations between the neutrino events and LHAASO sources, achieving the best p-values of 0.237, 0.312, and 0.115, respectively, for all LHAASO sources, KM2A sources, and WCDA sources. These findings imply that the spatial coincidence between LHAASO sources and neutrino alerts is relatively weak. Furthermore, under the assumption that gamma-rays are exclusively generated through hadronic interactions, we estimated the most optimistic theoretical neutrino fluxes from LHAASO sources and compared them with the IceCube observed fluxes. The results indicate that the majority of these sources are improbable counterparts to the detected neutrinos. In conclusion, LHAASO sources could be potential galactic neutrino emitters but currently do not exhibit compelling evidence, thereby underscoring the necessity for elevated sensitivity levels in forthcoming detection instruments like IceCube-Gen2.

papers.title: Development and characterization of a millimeter-wave circular polarization observation method using a quarter-wave plate with Simons Array
papers.abstract: We have developed and demonstrated a method for measuring circular polarization at 90 GHz by combining a quarter-wave plate (QWP) and a continuously rotating half-wave plate (HWP). While many bolometric experiments at millimeter wavelengths focus on measuring linear polarization, observations of circular polarization in millimeter waves may open a new window into astrophysics and cosmology. We present a novel approach to circular-polarization search using linear-polarization-sensitive detectors by incorporating a QWP in the optics. The Simons Array was originally designed for precise linear polarization measurements, and we subsequently installed a QWP in front of the receiver targeting 90 GHz. The QWP converts incident circular polarization to linear polarization, allowing detection with our detectors. Laboratory measurements demonstrate a QWP conversion efficiency of 99.0%. We apply our method to observations of unpolarized and linearly polarized bright sources, Jupiter and Tau A. Using these observations, we establish the calibration and characterize the instrumental leakages relevant to circular polarization measurements. The measured polarization efficiency adopted for Stokes $V$ is $46\pm2$%, and the measured U-to-V leakage is $-11.7\pm5.1$%. We measure a circular polarization fraction of $V/I=0.78\pm0.42$% for Tau A, showing no significant detection and providing a consistency check of the calibration and systematic-uncertainty treatment. These results establish the instrument response model and calibration parameters used for the companion circular-polarization source search.

papers.title: Cosmology with strong gravitational lenses
papers.abstract: Three of the most pressing open questions in cosmology -- the nature of dark energy and dark matter, and the growing tension in the value of the Hubble constant H$_0$ -- call for cosmological probes that are independent of, and complementary to, traditional methods. Strong gravitational lensing offers exactly that: a purely gravitational probe of the universe's expansion history and matter distribution, sensitive to dark matter's presence regardless of whether it interacts with light. Time-delay lenses and multiplane lenses can measure H$_0$ and the dark energy equation of state directly, while the distortion of lensed images can reveal the abundance and internal structure of dark matter subhalos. After a brief theoretical and historical introduction, I review recent breakthroughs enabled by JWST and by advances in lens modeling and stellar dynamics. Examples include the recent measurement of H$_0$ with 3\% precision in flat $Λ$ cold dark matter cosmology, and a tentative detection of dark matter self-interaction. Strong lensing is entering a pivotal era: wide-field surveys with Euclid, Rubin, and Roman, and radio surveys with the Square Kilometer Array, are poised to increase the number of known strong lenses by orders of magnitude, positioning strong lensing to play a central role in answering these open questions in the decade ahead.

papers.title: A possible evolutionary connection between high-mass X-ray binary pulsars and isolated rotation-powered pulsars
papers.abstract: We investigate the long-term spin evolution of high-mass X-ray binary (HMXB) pulsars in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) using archival measurements of spin periods and period derivatives from XMM-Newton, Chandra, and RXTE. In the P-|dP/dt| plane, the HMXB pulsars follow an approximately linear relation in log-log space with a slope of 1.02 +/- 0.11, similar to the trend shown by the youngest isolated rotation-powered pulsars (RPPs; e.g., Manchester et al., 2005; Lorimer and Kramer, 2005). For comparison, young RPPs from the ATNF Pulsar Catalogue give slopes that depend strongly on the characteristic-age cut: 1.10 +/- 0.16 for characteristic ages below 10,000 years and 0.72 +/- 0.08 for characteristic ages below 100,000 years. The full non-recycled population shows no significant correlation. The HMXB pulsars lie in the same characteristic-age range (approximately 1,000-10,000 years) as the youngest RPPs, but at spin periods two to three orders of magnitude longer. Reference characteristic-age contours in the HMXB P-|dP/dt| plane are roughly parallel to this relation, consistent with a continuous evolutionary sequence.

papers.title: Radion/Dilaton portal freeze-in dark matter in extra-dimensional theories
papers.abstract: We perform a comprehensive analysis of a radion/dilaton portal freeze-in dark matter in models of stabilized warped extra-dimensions. We show that the relic abundance of a generic dark matter particle (scalars, vectors, or fermions) is obtained via the conformal coupling of the radial mode in a consistent model stabilized warped extra- dimensions; our calculations show that in scenarios where the reheating temperature is much smaller than the radion mass, keV-TeV scale dark matter particles can saturate the relic density. We perform a comprehensive analysis of a radion/dilaton portal freeze-in dark matter in models of stabilized warped extra-dimensions. We show that the relic abundance of a generic dark matter particle (scalars, vectors, or fermions) is obtained via the conformal coupling of the radial mode in a consistent model stabilized warped extra- dimensions; our calculations show that in scenarios where the reheating temperature is much smaller than the radion mass, keV-TeV scale dark matter particles can saturate the relic density. Furthermore, we show that the model is subject to Lyman-alpha constraints in the keV-GeV range, providing a unique, model-independent probe of this sector. Our calculations extend previous attempts to calculate the freeze-in relic abundance in extra-dimensional portals by providing a consistent theoretical calculation of matrix elements, clearly laying out the underlying motivation and assumptions and providing a comprehensive account of the cosmological constraints on the model.

papers.title: Barflow: Modeling Gas Kinematics of Bar-Driven Flows
papers.abstract: We present self-consistent $N$-body/hydrodynamical simulations of isolated, Milky Way-like galaxies with stellar and gaseous disks. By varying the initial gas fraction, we find that gas delays bar formation and, in the most gas-rich model, suppresses it by exciting higher-order spiral modes and promoting early central mass growth. Once a bar forms, continued gas inflow and gravitational torques weaken the bar and inhibit its secular slowdown, keeping bars in the gas-bearing models shorter and predominantly in the fast-bar regime, while the gas-free bar evolves into the slow-bar regime. Stars and gas respond differently to the same barred potential. While the mean stellar velocity field is well described by a smooth bisymmetric pattern, the cold and warm gas follow elongated, $x_1$-like streamlines with sharp shock-induced velocity transitions, producing sawtooth-like radial and archlike tangential velocity profiles. Despite these strong noncircular motions, their azimuthally averaged tangential velocities closely follow the circular velocity over most of the disk. By contrast, the hot gas is dominated by stellar feedback and thermal pressure and is largely decoupled from the ordered bar-driven flow. To describe these bar-driven gas flows, we introduce the barflow model, a phenomenological description of non-sinusoidal gas streaming motions with a radially varying shock-front phase. Mock line-of-sight velocity-fitting experiments show that the barflow model recovers the intrinsic rotation curve, bar-driven velocity perturbations, and radial gas transport more accurately than the conventional bisymmetric model.

papers.title: Optimal Design of Shaped Pupil Lyot Coronagraph for China's Large Segmented Telescope
papers.abstract: China's next-generation large telescopes, such as the Expandable Aperture Segmented Telescope (EAST) and the Large Optical/Infrared Telescope (LOT), are being planned as flagship facilities for high-angular-resolution astronomy, including the direct imaging and characterization of exoplanetary systems (e.g., exoplanets, circumstellar disks). However, their segmented, centrally obscured apertures present significant challenges for coronagraph design: diffraction from segmented gaps and spiders severely limit contrast, particularly at small inner working angles (IWAs). To address this, we investigate an optimal Shaped Pupil Lyot Coronagraph (SPLC) architecture tailored for these telescopes, which combines a binary shaped pupil apodizer, a focal-plane occulting mask, and a Lyot stop to suppress stellar glare and enhance contrast. We further augment the coronagraph design with a two-deformable-mirror (2-DM) adaptive optics (AO) system to correct atmospheric turbulence and residual aberrations. End-to-end simulations based on site parameters for Lenghu in Qinghai Province and assuming idealized extreme AO (ExAO) correction demonstrate that the optimized 2DM-SPLC designs can achieve raw contrasts of order 10^-6-10^-7 in the V, H, and K bands, providing an upper-bound estimate of the system performance. The simulated performance highlights the advantages of the SPLC in mitigating diffraction from segmented and centrally obscured pupils while maintaining a small IWA and practical throughput, indicating that the 2DM-SPLC is a promising coronagraphic architecture for high-contrast exoplanet imaging on China's future large segmented telescopes.

papers.title: Magnetically Charged Black Holes from Grand Unified Theory
papers.abstract: Grand Unified models of particle physics inevitably give rise to magnetic monopoles. Often the model will also contain a weakly broken discrete symmetry that leads to the formation of biased domain walls that survive for a limited period in cosmology. For a range of the discrete symmetry breaking parameter, domain walls can collapse to form magnetically charged extremal black holes lighter than $\simeq 1\, {\rm kg}$ but these are not expected to survive until the present epoch due to Hawking evaporation and Schwinger pair production of monopoles. If the parameter is smaller still, the black holes may be astrophysical, with mass greater than $10^{15}\, {\rm g}$ and with sub-extremal magnetic charge: $Q \simeq 10^8$ (for our canonical choice of parameters). The cosmological energy density in residual magnetic monopoles depends on the discrete symmetry breaking parameter and for sufficiently small values of the parameter, the magnetic monopole density can satisfy all observational constraints.

papers.title: Simulations of Dust Content and Attenuation in $z=5-15$ Galaxies
papers.abstract: Correctly modeling the dust attenuation law in galaxies is essential to properly inferring their growth and physical properties. With the rapid discovery of $z>6$ galaxies by JWST and lack of constraints on the properties of dust at these redshifts, we must turn to theoretical models to predict the properties of dust at these redshifts. In this paper, we develop a theoretical foundation for the nature of high-redshift attenuation laws. We analyze $107$ cosmological zoom-in simulations of galaxies run with the SMUGGLE galaxy formation model. SMUGGLE includes an explicitly modeled multiphase interstellar medium and a state-of-the-art dust model with a self-consistently evolving dust grain size distribution. We forward model these simulations with the radiative transfer package POWDERDAY to produce synthetic spectra and attenuation curves for a set of $z=5-15$, $M_*\sim10^{6.5}-10^{10}\; \mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ galaxies. We find evidence for flatter attenuation curves than the commonly used locally-calibrated literature attenuation laws assumed when modeling high-redshift galaxies. The vast majority of our attenuation curves also lack the 2175 Angstrom absorption feature. Our attenuation laws do not evolve strongly over $z=15-5$, which we attribute to relatively constant fractions of small grains up to $z=4$ in our simulations. We present a set of simulation-informed priors on dust attenuation law parameterization that could be implemented in SED fitting codes. There is an anti-correlation between galaxy mass and attenuation curve slope and positive correlation between galaxy mass and $A_V$, which we attribute to dust growth becoming efficient in our massive galaxies with $\log{M_*/\mathrm{M}_{\odot}}\gtrsim9$ and with ISM conditions above a critical metallicity threshold.

papers.title: Emission spectroscopy of KELT-2A b with Gemini-North/IGRINS-2: hints of a stellar C/O ratio and sub-stellar metallicity
papers.abstract: We present the results of high-resolution emission spectroscopy of the hot Jupiter KELT-2A~b using IGRINS-2 on the Gemini-North telescope, covering the $H$- and $K$-bands at a spectral resolution of $R \sim 45{,}000$. Observations were carried out over five nights, covering both pre- and post-eclipse orbital phases. Stellar and telluric contaminations are removed via singular value decomposition. We detect $\rm H_2O$ at a signal-to-noise ratio of {6.57}, confirming the previous result at a higher significance. While $\rm ^{12}CO$ is identified in the log-likelihood map near the expected planetary velocity, a definitive detection of $\rm ^{12}CO$ remains elusive given the current data quality. We perform atmospheric retrieval both with IGRINS-2 data alone and jointly with archival \textit{Spitzer}/IRAC photometric data points. The retrieved temperature--pressure profile is non-inverted, consistent with prior observations. {From the joint fit we constrain the water abundance to} $\rm log(H_2O) = {-3.78^{+0.27}_{-0.20}}$ {with the free chemistry model}. {The chemical equilibrium model yields} $\rm C/O={ 0.19^{+0.12}_{-0.07}}$, $\rm [C/H]=-0.81^{+0.41}_{-0.34}$, and $\rm [O/H] = -0.37^{+0.27}_{-0.17}${: the C/O ratio agrees with the stellar value, while the carbon and oxygen abundances are moderately depleted relative to the host star, though still consistent at the $\sim2σ$ level.} If confirmed, {this combination of a stellar C/O ratio with a sub-stellar metallicity is difficult to reconcile with gas accretion between the $\rm{H_2O}$ and CO snowlines, which predicts a super-stellar C/O. It instead points to the accretion of metal-depleted gas outside the CO snowline with only limited planetesimal enrichment, and hence to a disk-free, high-eccentricity migration history.}

papers.title: Magnetic Reconnection Governs the Entire Lifecycle of Solar Eruptive Magnetic Flux Rope
papers.abstract: While magnetic flux ropes (MFRs) are widely accepted to exist prior to many solar eruptions, the physical mechanism responsible for triggering and subsequently driving their eruptions remains debated. Classical models commonly attribute eruption onset to ideal magnetohydrodynamic instabilities, particularly the torus instability, while magnetic reconnection is often regarded as a secondary process. Using high-resolution three-dimensional MHD simulations, we investigate the eruption of an MFR that forms self-consistently through flux cancellation driven by converging motions and photospheric diffusion following an initial shearing phase. The pre-eruption MFR rises quasi-statically and reaches a height where the decay index exceeds the classical torus instability threshold, yet the system continues to evolve quasi-statically without eruption. Instead, eruption begins only when the current sheet beneath the MFR becomes sufficiently thin for magnetic reconnection to set in. Increasing numerical resolution systematically delays the eruption onset, whereas the decay index at eruption onset remains nearly unchanged, demonstrating that the onset is governed by reconnection rather than torus instability. During the eruption, magnetic reconnection continuously converts surrounding sheared arcades into newly reconnected twisted flux that merges with the pre-eruption MFR and continuously to build the erupting MFR. A component-resolved analysis of the Lorentz force work further shows that the newly reconnection flux contributes predominantly to the main acceleration phase. These results demonstrate that magnetic reconnection plays a central role throughout the entire lifecycle of the eruptive MFR: it builds the MFR, directly triggers its eruption, and provides the dominant driving of the eruption.

papers.title: Search for Sub-Solar Mass Binaries in the First and Second Part of LIGO's Fourth Observing Run O4a-O4b
papers.abstract: The observation of sub-solar mass neutron stars and black holes would signify a new class of astrophysical objects since these systems are not expected to form via standard stellar evolution. We present the first sub-solar mass search for binaries consisting of neutron star or black holes that uses the data from both the second part (O4b) and first part (O4a) of the fourth observing run of the Advanced LIGO detectors. The search covers primary masses 0.1 to 2 $M_\odot$ and secondary masses 0.1 to 1 $M_\odot$. Tidal effects up to $7\times10^5$ are accounted for in extremely low-mass neutron stars. No statistically significant candidates are identified. We place a $90\%$ confidence upper limit on the merger rate $\mathcal{R}_{90}$ for sub-solar mass black holes and neutron stars to be $< 5.2\times10^{2}\,\textrm{Gpc}^{-3}\,\textrm{yr}^{-1}$ for a chirp mass of 0.5 $M_\odot$, a factor $2.2 \times$ lower compared to previous O1-O4a searches. We constrain the effective local dark matter fraction to be $\tilde{f}_\textrm{PBH}<0.6\%$ for $M_{\textrm{PBH}}=0.8 \,M_\odot$, approximately $1.5$ factor improvement to previous O1-O4a constraints. Given our model assumptions, our local dark matter fraction constraints are $2-7$ times lower than the OGLE microlensing survey for $M_{\textrm{PBH}}\ge{0.6}~M_\odot$.

papers.title: ExoEcho: Exoplanet Ephemerides Change Observations. III. A JWST Survey for Transit Timing Variations of 37 Exoplanets
papers.abstract: Transit timing variations (TTVs) provide a powerful probe of planetary dynamics and orbital evolution. We extend the ExoEcho project by incorporating James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) transit observations and analyze 84 light curves of 37 exoplanets, including 20 hot Jupiters, 11 Neptune-like planets, and 6 super-Earths. We derive updated transit ephemerides and conduct a systematic search for long-term and periodic TTV signals. We identify two strong TTV candidates, including HATS-6~b and HAT-P-18~b. The hot Jupiter HATS-6~b exhibits a long-term trend with $\dot{P} = 230.5 \pm 46.8\ \mathrm{ms\ yr^{-1}}$, potentially driven by tidal interactions with its host star. In addition, the Neptune-like planet HAT-P-18~b shows periodic TTV signal with amplitude of $92.9 \pm 13.7$~s. We also show that the previously claimed positive period derivative in WASP-121~b is inconsistent with our new transit timing data. Although continued monitoring is required to confirm these findings, our results demonstrate the potential of JWST for high-precision transit timing and extend TTV studies beyond the traditional hot-Jupiter population to lower-mass exoplanets.

papers.title: Large-scale Environmental Dependence of AGN Activity Revealed by JWST Pa$α$ Emitters
papers.abstract: The role of the large-scale environment in regulating AGN activity remains an open question. We investigate the Mpc-scale environments of 70 AGNs at $z=1.1$-$1.5$ using a highly complete sample of 3,419 Pa$α$ emitters with accurate spectroscopic redshifts from JWST slitless spectroscopic survey. This dataset allows us to robustly trace the environments and quantify the environmental dependence of AGN properties. We measure the eighth-nearest-neighbor surface density of Pa$α$ emitters around each AGN, probing $\sim$1.5 pMpc scale environments. We find that this environmental density exhibits a weak positive correlation with radio luminosity. Radio-bright AGNs tend to reside in statistically denser environments than their radio-faint counterparts. The environmental density also has a positive correlation with the Eddington ratio and a weak negative correlation with the central black hole mass, implying more efficient black hole accretion in dense environments. We construct Pa$α$ luminosity functions (LFs) in AGN environments and find that they are systematically elevated relative to the field Pa$α$ LF. In addition, their faint-end slopes are shallower, suggesting accelerated galaxy growth and enhanced quenching of star formation. As Pa$α$ emitters trace gas-rich, star-forming galaxies, our results support a scenario in which the large-scale cold gas promotes AGN activity at cosmic noon.

papers.title: Hot Molecular Hydrogen in Galaxies at Redshift ~ 0.2-1.5 Revealed by JWST
papers.abstract: Molecular hydrogen (H$_2$) is the fundamental component of the molecular gas reservoir that fuels star formation and black hole growth. While prominent hot H$_2$ emission ($\gtrsim 1000$ K) has been explored in nearby galaxies, its excitation mechanisms at higher redshifts remain poorly constrained. We present a systematic study of hot molecular gas traced via ro-vibrational H$_2$ emitters at z~0.2-1.5 using JWST slitless spectroscopy. Exploiting JWST's great sensitivity to near-infrared H$_2$ ro-vibrational transitions such as H$_2$ 1-0 S(1), we build a sample of 144 H$_2$-luminous galaxies and characterize their multi-wavelength properties. About 96.5% and 80% of these galaxies are detected in the radio and far-infrared (FIR) bands, respectively, and their hot H$_2$ emission strongly correlates with the radio and FIR radiation. Based on radio excess, X-ray emission, and optical diagnostics, 62 sources (43%) exhibit significant AGN activity. The H$_2$ line luminosities of the sample show a sublinear dependence on radio luminosity, while the relation between the H$_2$ luminosities and total infrared luminosities is approximately linear after excluding the radio-excess sources. These scaling relations suggest that star formation provides a baseline contribution to hot H$_2$ excitation, while radio-excess sources require an additional contribution from AGN-related processes such as jet- or wind-driven shocks. These results reveal a multi-channel excitation scenario and shed new light on the interplay between star formation, AGN activity, and the interstellar medium during galaxy evolution.

papers.title: A JWST View of Cosmic Star Formation from $z\sim0$ to 9 with Hydrogen Recombination Lines in the COSMOS and GOODS-N fields
papers.abstract: We combine wide-area COSMOS-3D observations with deeper GOODS-N data from JWST/NIRCam F444W wide-field slitless spectroscopy to trace cosmic star formation over $z\sim0$--9. The observations cover approximately $0.33~\mathrm{deg}^2$ in COSMOS and $60.9~\mathrm{arcmin}^2$ in GOODS-N, with typical $3σ$ integrated line-flux limits of $3.2\times10^{-18}$ and $1.04\times10^{-18}~\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,cm^{-2}}$, respectively. The common $3.9$--$5.0\,μ$m wavelength window probes Br$α$, Br$β$, Pa$α$, Pa$β$, H$α$, and H$β$ across the local Universe, cosmic noon, and reionization. Our final sample contains 9146 galaxies, including 7883 in COSMOS and 1263 in GOODS-N. COSMOS constrains luminous emitters, while GOODS-N extends the luminosity functions toward fainter sources. We measure dust-corrected line luminosities, account for line-detection completeness, and convert the six lines to equivalent H$α$ luminosities assuming Case B recombination. Schechter fits reveal an increase in the characteristic H$α$-equivalent luminosity toward cosmic noon. Integrating the resulting star formation rate functions above $0.24\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, we trace the cosmic star formation rate density from the local Universe to reionization. The combined Brackett, Paschen, and Balmer measurements are broadly consistent with the canonical UV- and IR-based cosmic star formation history at $z\lesssim6$. Fixed-slope tests show that the H$β$ estimate at $z\sim8$ remains sensitive to the external photometric faint-end constraint and extrapolation below our spectroscopic limit. These measurements provide complementary constraints on the distribution and integrated rate of star formation across cosmic time.

papers.title: Deep X-ray View of a Distant Protocluster Anchored by a Quasar at $z=6.63$: No Evidence for Enhanced X-ray AGN Activity
papers.abstract: Whether dense environments accelerate SMBH growth during cosmic reionization remains uncertain because X-ray constraints on $z>6$ protoclusters are rare. We analyze $\sim865$ ks of Chandra observations of J0910-0414 quasar field, a massive protocluster at $z=6.63$. We construct a catalog of 251 X-ray sources and search for AGN among 21 spectroscopically confirmed members, excluding the central quasar. This is the first systematic X-ray AGN census in a $z>6$ protocluster; none of the members is individually detected. Stacking all members ($\sim17$ Ms total exposure) yields no significant signal and limits the average rest-frame 2-10 keV luminosity to $\langle L_{\rm 2-10~keV}\rangle\leq9.54\times10^{42}~\rm erg~s^{-1}$. The null result gives a central 90% Jeffreys upper bound of $f_{\rm AGN}<0.09$. After accounting for the spatially varying sensitivity, the field Compton-thin X-ray luminosity function predicts $N_{\rm exp,field}=0.0356$ AGN in the surveyed volume. Assuming the overdensity profile of AGNs in this protocluster is the same as that of galaxies determined by Wang et al. (2024), the expected AGN count becomes $N_{\rm exp}=0.131$. Zero detections then imply a one-sided 90% upper limit of $η_{\rm rel}<17.5$ on any additional X-ray AGN enhancement beyond that associated with the galaxy overdensity. Although $η_{\rm rel}<17.5$ permits more than an order-of-magnitude enhancement, the data show no significant excess of X-ray-detectable AGN in J0910-0414 protocluster. The present X-ray data may miss heavily obscured, intrinsically X-ray-weak, or intermittently accreting SMBHs; the non-detection therefore does not rule out AGNs among the member galaxies.

papers.title: Transients and Stellar Activity as Revealed by Ultraviolet Diagnostic Tracers
papers.abstract: Ultraviolet (UV) observations offer unique insights into transient and variable astrophysical phenomena, from the Sun and nearby stars to supernovae and star-forming galaxies. Here, we summarise and review the diagnostic power of the UV spectrum for probing the physical conditions, dynamics and energetics of these events. We trace the historical development of UV astronomy from early satellite missions to the current landscape shaped by the Hubble Space Telescope, the GALaxy Evolution eXplorer, the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory and AstroSat/UVIT. Particular emphasis is placed on resonance lines such as Mg II $h$ and $k$, C II, Si IV, C IV and N V, which probe the (solar and) stellar chromosphere and transition region, revealing magnetic heating, shocks and mass loss across stellar types. We examine UV diagnostics of stellar flares, pre-main-sequence activity and rotation--activity correlations, linking them to exoplanetary irradiation and habitability. We then explore the UV view of supernova shock breakout and early-time emission, as well as the far-UV mapping of young stellar populations and hierarchical star formation in the Magellanic Clouds. Together, these aspects illustrate how the UV connects small-scale plasma processes to galactic-scale star formation. Despite remarkable progress, UV transient astronomy remains limited by instrument availability and cadence. Forthcoming missions promise to transform this field by capturing the rapid, luminous phenomena that define the dynamic Universe.

papers.title: The Contribution of Mergers and Accretion to Dark Matter Halo Assembly: An Excursion Set Theory Approach
papers.abstract: We study the relative contributions of mergers and accretion to the assembly of dark matter haloes within the framework of Excursion Set Theory (EST). We extend a variance-discretized merger-tree algorithm, which recursively reconstructs all branches of a complete merger tree and introduces a merger-ratio criterion for distinguishing mergers from accretion. The method is validated by comparing the resulting progenitor distributions with the analytical conditional first up-crossing distribution, showing excellent agreement over a wide range of halo masses and redshifts. We find that the accretion contribution depends strongly on the adopted merger-ratio threshold. For large merger ratios ($MR=0.1$--$0.25$), accretion accounts for up to $\sim70\%$ of the mass growth of massive haloes, whereas including all resolved mergers ($MR=10^{-6}$) reduces the accretion contribution to $\sim40\%$. These values are in good agreement with previous N-body simulation results. The accreted mass exhibits a nearly self-similar distribution in the mass-redshift plane, with the dominant contribution arising from progenitors in the range $10^{-3}M_0 \lesssim M \lesssim 10^{-1}M_0$ and predominantly at $0.5 \lesssim z \lesssim 2$. Our results demonstrate that EST-based merger trees provide an accurate and computationally efficient framework for investigating halo assembly and quantifying the relative roles of mergers and accretion in hierarchical structure formation.

papers.title: Twisted Pseudodisk and Asymmetric Mass Accretion on the Circumstellar Disk II: Parameter Survey
papers.abstract: Using three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations accounting for ohmic dissipation, we investigate the long-term evolution of the infalling envelope for $\sim 100,000$\,yr after protostar formation. The primary control parameter is the initial misalignment angle $θ_0$ between the rotation axis and the magnetic field, varied from $0^\circ$ to $90^\circ$. In all misaligned models ($θ_0 \ne 0^\circ$), the pseudodisk (or infalling envelope) surrounding the circumstellar disk develops a highly distorted and complex morphology. Gas accretion from the envelope proceeds through discrete, channel-like flows, producing asymmetric streams rather than axisymmetric infall. Protostellar outflows are launched even in these complex environments, and inflow and outflow regions are strongly interwoven. Outflows transport angular momentum anisotropically, leading to time-dependent changes in disk orientation and outflow direction, which further enhance envelope asymmetry. We examine the relative orientation between gas flows and magnetic fields and find that, although statistical tendencies exist, accretion streams cannot be uniquely characterized as either parallel or perpendicular to the magnetic field, particularly in strongly misaligned cases. We also show that most infalling gas accretes at nearly the free-fall velocity, with only a minor fraction significantly slowed within the pseudodisk. Asymmetric accretion and stream-like structures persist beyond 10,000\,au, demonstrating that large-scale asymmetry can arise intrinsically. Our results show that complex streams and asymmetric envelopes naturally emerge from magnetized core physics, even in the absence of initial turbulence or external gas accretion.

papers.title: The Limits of Tidal Circularization and Atmospheric Escape for Mini-Neptunes and Super-Earths: The Case of TOI-2257 b
papers.abstract: With a 35-day orbital period and $\sim$0.5 eccentricity, TOI-2257 b occupies a sparsely populated corner of transiting mini-Neptune parameter space and may lie near the orbital distance at which tidal and atmospheric escape process become negligible. To test this hypothesis, we performed simulations of the combined stellar, tidal, and atmospheric evolution and confirmed that TOI-2257 b does lie near this boundary, regardless of whether it formed with or without a primordial hydrogen envelope. In the mini-Neptune scenario, we find that all cases retain an envelope of at least 0.02 M$_\oplus$ for 8 Gyr, but that the envelope mass can be halved if it was initially larger than 0.2 M$_\oplus$. We find that tidal evolution only occurs for cases with initial envelope masses larger than 0.02 M$_\oplus$ because their radii are large enough to generate significant torques. In the super-Earth scenario, the planet could lose $\sim$10 Earth ocean masses of surface water during the $\sim$75 Myr pre-main sequence and therefore could be habitable if it formed with $\gtrsim$2x Earth's surface water mass. The predicted tidal heating surface flux tends to be similar to Io, with no cases approaching the flux required to drive a runaway greenhouse. We find that if the planet is rocky, then eccentricities larger than 0.62 today are strongly disfavored, implying that larger eccentricities could confirm the gaseous nature of the planet. These results suggest that TOI-2257 b could provide valuable constraints on mini-Neptune properties and new insight into the radius valley shape as a function of eccentricity.

papers.title: Tracing Accretion and Inner-Disk Gas Evolution in the Orion Nebula via Br-alpha and CO
papers.abstract: We present a systematic spectroscopic study of hydrogen Brackett-alpha (Br-alpha) and carbon monoxide (CO) fundamental-band (4.3-5.2 micron) emission from a homogeneous sample of 0.2-1.5 Msun pre-main-sequence (PMS) stars in the Orion Nebula observed with JWST/NIRSpec-MOS as part of our Chandra-JWST project. Using 73 Br-alpha and 46 CO spectra, we investigate correlations between warm-gas emission, stellar properties, accretion, and environment with censored correlation and regression analyses accounting for multiple testing. Br-alpha luminosity correlates strongly with accretion luminosity (Lacc), even after excluding sources within 2' of Theta1 Ori C, the nebula's main ionizing O-type star, whose radiation may bias proplyd Lacc estimates. This supports Br-alpha as a robust empirical tracer of accretion in PMS stars. Br-alpha also correlates with visual extinction (Av) and more weakly with stellar bolometric luminosity and mass. CO fundamental-band luminosities likewise correlate positively with Lacc and Av, relationships that persist in a larger combined JWST/NIRSpec+MIRI sample spanning multiple star-forming regions. In contrast to Br-alpha, CO luminosity shows no significant dependence on basic stellar properties, suggesting that warm molecular gas is governed primarily by accretion and local disk conditions. The weaker correlations of the Spitzer/IRAC spectral slope with Lacc and Av suggest that warm inner-disk gas may evolve or disperse faster than optically thick dust. Overall, the CO results tentatively indicate declining warm-gas emission as disks evolve, modulated by accretion-powered thermal and ultraviolet excitation, although variations in emitting area inherited from natal core conditions may also contribute.

papers.title: Paleo-heat flux estimates across Enceladus derived from flexural response of the ice shell
papers.abstract: Saturn's moon Enceladus has active plumes suggestive of locally high heat fluxes at present, and the present-day heating is reasonably well characterized. However, the moon's thermal history is not well understood. In this study, we model flexural deformation of chasmata and dorsae in various regions of Enceladus to find the effective elastic thickness of the ice shell and constrain temporal and spatial variations in heat flux. We find paleo-heat fluxes of 60-$\geq$350 mWm$^{-2}$, with most clustered around 125-200 mWm$^{-2}$. Present day measured heat fluxes at the South Polar Terrain (SPT) are comparable to our estimated paleo-heat fluxes in non-SPT regions. Our paleo-heat fluxes, however, are significantly higher than the corresponding present day heat fluxes for the same locations inferred from shell thickness maps. This suggests that regions outside the SPT experienced a past episode of heating (heat fluxes in excess of 100mWm$^{-2}$) followed by a cooling and thickening ice shell. A relatively constant paleo-heat flux for terrains of different ages (determined from crater densities) supports the "resonance locking" hypothesis of dissipation in Saturn and might imply a long-lived resonance between Enceladus and Dione. Our results suggest that Enceladus's tidal heating appears to have been consistent over time. Consistent peak heating at Enceladus could support a long-lived subsurface ocean, which has important consequences for astrobiology and the habitability of the outer solar system.

papers.title: Chandra-JWST Probing the Effects of Moderate X-Ray Superflares on Protoplanetary Disks
papers.abstract: Powerful X-ray flares from young stars may rapidly alter the physical and chemical conditions of their planet-forming disks, but direct observational tests remain scarce. We present a Chandra-JWST/NIRSpec study of infrared spectral variability associated with pre-main-sequence (PMS) X-ray flares in the Orion Nebula. Combining six Chandra/ACIS-I observations with three NIRSpec-MOS visits, we analyze two-epoch spectra of 10 X-ray Flare stars and 12 matched non-flaring Controls among 84 observed disk-bearing PMS stars. We investigate three diagnostics: narrow 2.8-4.3 micron features, HI Br-alpha, and the CO fundamental band. Flare stars show tentative evidence for relatively fewer variable narrow features at longer wavelengths than Controls, while feature incidence decreases strongly with projected distance from the dominant ionizing O star Theta1 Ori C. Most classifiable features appear in absorption. These properties suggest that at least some features may arise in externally irradiated disk atmospheres and/or associated photoevaporative flows, with their apparent epoch-to-epoch variability potentially reflecting spatial sampling of such locally structured material rather than intrinsic temporal changes. Br-alpha behaves differently: flare stars show systematically stronger variability and uniquely exhibit absorption-core profiles, suggesting control by magnetospheric accretion and stellar magnetic processes rather than disk irradiation. The CO fundamental band shows no significant flare-associated variability, consistent with thermochemical models predicting weak responses to moderate X-ray superflares. This pilot study demonstrates the potential of coordinated Chandra-JWST observations to probe how young stellar magnetic activity affects planet-forming environments, motivating future monitoring to build larger superflare samples and extend them into the rare X-ray mega-flare regime.

papers.title: Studying the Near-horizon Jet of M87 using Millimeter Balloon-borne VLBI stations
papers.abstract: In this paper we present synthetic Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) observations of M87 between a near-future configuration of the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) and one or multiple 2.5 m-class balloon-borne VLBI stations on a northern transatlantic flight trajectory launching from Kiruna, Sweden. These balloon-borne VLBI stations have the advantage of operating above 99.5% of the atmosphere and their motion allows for efficient sampling of the uv-plane. Assuming frequency phase transfer between 230 and 86 GHz we run these simulations using a modified version of the ngehtsim software package. Our simulations demonstrate the ability of such a VLBI array to probe M87 at the jet base adding baselines down to 0.2 G$λ$ for a single balloon-VLBI station and 0.07 G$λ$ for three balloon VLBI stations. Using the Bayesian imaging software Comrade.jl, we demonstrate the recovery of jet structures up to 150 $μ$as in size for a single balloon and up to 300 $μ$as in size with three balloons. Finally, we test the improvement in jet image fidelity by computing the normalized cross-correlation (NXCOR) and normalized-root-mean-square error (NRMSE) between the image reconstruction and ground truth. We find a factor of 1.2 improvement in the jet NRMSE for a single balloon and a factor of 1.3 improvement for 3 balloons as compared to EHT-only simulations.

papers.title: Galactic Outflows and Star-Formation Quenching: A JWST Perspective
papers.abstract: Outflows driven by active galactic nuclei (AGN) are widely considered a key mechanism for regulating and quenching star formation in massive galaxies. However, direct observational evidence linking outflows to quenching has remained elusive for decades. This article reviews recent findings for massive galaxies at cosmic noon ($z\sim 2$), based on sensitive James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations tracing both star formation histories (through Balmer absorption lines) and neutral outflows (through blueshifted NaID absorption). Neutral outflows are found in $\sim$ 25 - 50% of massive ($\log(M_*/M_\odot)>$ 10) galaxies, independent of star formation rate. Outflows from star-forming galaxies are consistent with being powered by star-formation and/or AGN activity, whereas outflows from quiescent systems are generally attributed to current or previous AGN activity. There is growing evidence that recent rapid quenching of star-formation is associated with powerful AGN-driven outflows with mass loading factors $η\gtrsim$ 1 - 10. The neutral gas dominates the outflow mass budget but in most cases its velocity is below the halo escape velocity, indicating that this gas may form part of a galactic fountain. Detections of neutral gas inflows and residual cold gas reservoirs in quiescent galaxies suggest that other feedback mechanisms such as AGN heating are required to keep galaxies quenched over long timescales. We highlight the potential of multiphase outflow measurements to constrain feedback models, describe the main systematic uncertainties in mass outflow rate measurements, and discuss how the $z\sim 2$ results inform our understanding of the formation of the earliest massive quiescent galaxies.

papers.title: Emergence of high-mass stars in complex fiber networks (EMERGE) VII. Multi-Tracer Column Density Synthesis
papers.abstract: Obtaining accurate estimates of the gas column density $\mathrm{N(H_2)}$ is crucial to determine the physical conditions of the molecular gas in the Interstellar Medium. This paper introduces the "Multi-Tracer Column Density Synthesis" (MT-CDS) technique, a new empirical approach to derive high dynamic-range column density maps with interferometers such as ALMA. We have compared the integrated intensity maps of two density selective tracers, namely HNC (1-0) and $\mathrm{N_2H^+}$ (1-0), obtained with IRAM-30m with ancillary Herschel column density estimates in seven star-forming regions in Orion and derived individual temperature-corrected conversion factors for each of these tracers. We applied these conversion factors obtained at low-resolution into similar high sensitivity ALMA observations to derive independent column density maps describing both the low $N_\mathrm{HNC}\mathrm{(H_2)}$ and high $N_\mathrm{N_2H^+}\mathrm{(H_2)}$ column density components at high spatial resolution (4.5"). We also combined these independent maps into estimates for the total gas column density gas $N_\mathrm{tot}\mathrm{(H_2)}$ sampling more than two orders of magnitude in column density between $\sim 10^{21.5}-10^{23.5}$ cm$^{-2}$. A comparison with independent ArTeMiS column density maps at intermediate resolution (8") shows typical deviations of $\lesssim$0.2 dex from our MT-CDS gas column density estimates. We obtained individual column density maps in five of our targets at $\sim$2000 au resolution in which ALMA observations were available, that is a factor of $\sim$5 better than originally calibrated. These results demonstrate the potential of this MT-CDS technique to retrieve accurate, high dynamic range $N\mathrm{(H_2)}$ total gas column density estimates at interferometric resolution combining multiple molecular line tracers.

papers.title: SQuIGGLE: Radio AGN Found Predominantly in Young, Gas-rich Post-starburst Galaxies at z ~ 0.7
papers.abstract: The processes that rapidly quench massive galaxies and maintain their quiescence remain poorly understood. Substantial molecular gas reservoirs can survive this shutdown in post-starburst galaxies, raising the question of what prevents the remaining gas from efficiently forming stars. We present deep, subarcsecond VLA 6 GHz observations of 52 massive SQuIGGLE post-starburst galaxies at $z\sim0.7$ to test the prevalence and mechanical impact of radio activity during the gas-rich post-burst phase. We detect 6 GHz continuum emission in 18/52 galaxies ($\approx$35\%), spanning $\log(L_{1.4\,{\rm GHz}}/{\rm W\,Hz^{-1}})\simeq23.0$--$25.0$ and generally exceeding the contributions expected from ongoing star formation and the fading starburst, favoring an AGN origin. Ancillary data at other wavelengths provide little evidence for a population of luminous, radiatively efficient AGN, suggesting that these sources are instead dominated by comparatively weak, mechanically powered radio AGN. Radio activity is strongly concentrated within the first $\sim$200 Myr post-burst and is predominantly associated with galaxies retaining substantial gas reservoirs. Above a common radio luminosity threshold, the radio detection fraction is enhanced by a factor of $\approx$2.5 relative to the radio AGN candidate fraction in mass- and redshift-matched quiescent LEGA-C galaxies, primarily due to lower power sources. For efficient jet--ISM coupling, the inferred mechanical power could supply the approximate energy required to unbind the molecular gas on timescales comparable to its observed decline. Together, these results identify a population of radiatively inefficient AGN hosted predominantly by young, gas-rich post-starburst galaxies at $z\sim0.7$ and suggest that they may have a role in maintaining inefficient star formation.

papers.title: Are Broad Mg II Galaxies Fading AGN?
papers.abstract: We analyzed a sample of 494 galaxies from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) I-IV that have unusual properties. They display broadened Mg II $λ$2798 line emission, as would be expected of Type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGN). However, they have weak or absent broad Balmer lines though broadened Balmer lines often accompany broadened ultraviolet lines in Type 1 AGN spectra. We performed a spectral decomposition of these "broad Mg II galaxies'' to assess whether they can be considered fading AGN. The Balmer lines are more responsive to changes in the AGN continuum than the Mg II line. As the AGN power source fades, broad H$β$ and then H$α$ will weaken and eventually disappear, leaving broad Mg II as a signpost of a more active past. In support of this interpretation, we found that broad Mg II galaxies have weaker AGN luminosities and lower accretion rates (parameterized by the Eddington ratio) than typical Type 1 quasars from SDSS. The Eddington ratio of broad Mg II galaxies are similar to dim-state changing-look AGN, with an average value $\lesssim$1\%, which is the threshold at which the inner region of a geometrically thin accretion disk is thought to evaporate and be replaced by a geometrically thick radiatively inefficient accretion flow in stellar-mass black holes. Broad Mg II galaxies may represent the penultimate stage in a changing-look AGN sequence prior to the complete disappearance of all broad lines.

papers.title: A Distinct Type of Standstill in Ultra-Compact White Dwarf Binaries
papers.abstract: AM CVn stars are ultra-compact, semi-detached binaries consisting of a white dwarf primary and a hydrogen-poor secondary. In this work, we analyse the AM CVn-type systems MGAB-V270, ZTF18aaxuusk and ASASSN-19ct, which have similar properties and show unusual post-superoutburst behaviour. We focus on the occurrence of standstill-like phases. In MGAB-V270, superoutbursts are followed by a series of echo outbursts that evolves into a standstill-like phase before the system returns to quiescence. ZTF18aaxuus shows similar post-superoutburst activity, with one echo-outburst series also developing into a standstill-like phase. ASASSN-19ct exhibits comparable echo outbursts but no standstill-like phases. Periodicity analysis using TESS data shows that superhumps can persist during both echo outbursts and standstill-like phases. Although standstills have previously been observed in AM CVn stars, the standstill-like phases we observe appear to represent a distinct phenomenon associated with post-superoutburst activity. We compare our results to other AM CVns that may exhibit similar behaviour.

papers.title: Understanding the Complex Morphology of a Coronal Mass Ejection. III: How to Create a Severe Geomagnetic Storm
papers.abstract: On April 21, 2023, a complex filament eruption produced an Earth-directed coronal mass ejection (CME) that triggered the first severe geomagnetic storm of solar cycle 25. The primary objective of this work is to understand the physical origin of the severe impact of this CME on Earth. We explore the CME's complex morphology by simulating the eruption using the thermodynamic magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) model CORHEL-CME. We model the pre-eruptive structure as two intertwined magnetic flux ropes and validate the early evolution of the event by comparing synthetic observables generated from the model with extreme-ultraviolet and white-light observations. We then compare the simulated CME structure with in situ measurements. From our analysis, we conclude that the CME merged with a stream interaction region (SIR) before reaching Earth. This interaction compressed the CME sheath, producing a sustained negative $B_n$ component that, together with the associated enhancement in solar wind density and velocity, triggered the geomagnetic storm. The internal configuration of the magnetic flux rope, which also maintained a sustained southward component during its propagation toward Earth, intensified the storm to severe levels. This model-data comparison underscores the power of using MHD simulations, when validated by multi-viewpoint observations, to reveal hidden dynamical processes and improve the understanding and prediction of space weather impacts.

papers.title: Science-Driven Performance Requirements for UV Coronagraph Design: Implications for O$_3$ Detection in Earth-like Atmospheres
papers.abstract: Detecting biosignatures on Earth-like exoplanets from the Proterozoic era requires instrumentation capable of probing near-ultraviolet (NUV) spectral features, particularly ozone (\ce{O3}), which serves as an indirect proxy for molecular oxygen (\ce{O2}) when direct detection is challenging. Using a combination of photochemical-climate modeling and atmospheric retrieval simulations, we quantify fiducial instrument performance requirements for robust \ce{O3} detection and assess the risk of spectral false positives from sulfur dioxide (\ce{SO2}). Our analysis demonstrates the \ce{O3} abundances for Proterozoic Earth-like planets with \ce{O2} as low as 0.1\% the present atmospheric level, can be constrained to within an order of magnitude at 1\,$σ$ confidence using three adjacent photometric bandpasses at a signal-to-noise ratio of 10 at 0.366\,$\upmu$m, each with a 15\% width, and a short wavelength cutoff for those observations near 0.26\,$\upmu$m. The self-consistent steady state atmospheric modeling results show that \ce{SO2} buildup is difficult in a habitable environment with appreciable amounts of water vapor in its atmosphere and would require volcanic outgassing rates at least two orders of magnitude above present-day Earth to reach surface abundance levels comparable to Proterozoic Earth-like abundances of \ce{O3}. Even under these high \ce{SO2} flux scenarios, \ce{SO2} remains largely unconstrained with the recommended observational configuration, reinforcing the need for NUV coverage in coronagraphic instruments. Our findings support the inclusion of UV-optimized optics and detectors on the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) to enable biosignature detection strategies sensitive to atmospheric conditions across key phases of Earth's geological history.

papers.title: MOSS III: MeerKATs view on the galaxy populations in two massive galaxy clusters
